disagreements.topic: GPU capex per $ of annual revenue for new and refreshed capacity (the main DCF driver)
disagreements.positions: A1 GPU $35-38.5m new / $32m refresh per $20m/MW (1.6-1.9x); A2 $36m per $20m (1.8x), pipeline $36m per $18m (2.0x); A3 $40m air / $34m liquid per $20m (2.0x / 1.7x), refresh $34-40m per $17m (2.0-2.35x), pipeline $34m per $18m (1.9x); A4 $45m per $20.6m (2.2x); A5 revenue/GPU capex 0.45 (2.2x). A4 at 1.8x would be +$47; A5 at 1.67x +$8.
disagreements.resolution: Settled at 2.2x of annual revenue for market-priced new and refreshed capacity, with 2.0x as the optimistic bound and 3.0x for hyperscaler-priced contracts. Every IREN deal sits at or above 2.0x: the 50k-B300 order (~$3.5bn incl. infrastructure) against the derived ~$1.56bn Mackenzie/Childress 2026 ARR gives 2.24x; Dell $1.6bn against NVIDIA's $0.68bn ARR gives 2.35x; Microsoft $5.81bn against $1.94bn gives 3.0x. Management's own claim is a ~2-year payback of compute investment at >$20m/MW (Q4 FY26 call; also Oct-2025 '~2-year revenue payback'), which is about 2.0x. The CEO also said current pricing reflects GPUs ordered earlier, while the CFO guides 15-20% higher per-MW GPU and DC cost. So 1.6-1.9x (A1, A2, and A3 on liquid and pipeline) is below every piece of evidence. At 2.2x a GPU cycle earns roughly WACC: my per-MW check gives a refresh NPV of about -$1m/MW (air, $20m) and -$3m/MW (liquid, ~$15.5m/MW at ~$34m GPU), against +$6-11m/MW in A1, A2 and A3. For liquid IT MW the ratio means about $15-16m revenue on about $34m GPU (Microsoft $29m/MW plus inflation), which is what A5 uses. A1, A2 and A3 pair $20m with $34-36m.
disagreements.evidence: Q4 FY26 call (stockanalysis transcript): '>$20 million per megawatt of IT load, paying back the compute investment in around 2 years'; capex up 15-20%; Mar-4-2026 release (>50k B300, ~$3.5bn H2-2026 GPU and infrastructure capex); Dell 8-K/release May-26-2026 ($1.6bn; ARR $3.7bn -> $4.4bn); Nov-2025 Microsoft 8-K ($9.7bn/5y, $5.8bn GPUs).

disagreements.positions: A4 $1.5bn/yr fixed plus 8% variable, DC maintenance and repairs (steady-state EBITDA margin about 62%); A1 17% of revenue plus 3% SBC on top of $2.5m/MW site cost (~67% incl. SBC); A2 17% of revenue plus $2.2m/MW (~72%); A3 $0.25bn/yr but EBITDA = 80% of revenue less $1.6m/MW (~70%); A5 15% SG&A plus $2.5m/MW (~70%).
disagreements.resolution: Settled at about $1.0-1.2bn/yr of cash corporate cost at FY29+ scale (about 9% of revenue), FY27 about $0.5bn, giving a steady-state EBITDA margin of about 70% on market-priced capacity. Q4 FY26 GAAP SG&A was $128.3m (about $86m cash after ~$42m SBC from the EBITDA bridge), with Q1 FY27 cash SG&A guided +$40-50m q/q, so about $0.5bn/yr today on about $1bn of operating ARR. CoreWeave's 2025 S&M + G&A was 15.5% of revenue on a GAAP basis including heavy post-IPO SBC, or roughly 9-10% in cash. A3's $0.25bn line looks low, but its 20%-of-revenue haircut covers overhead in total. Only A4 is outside the range; its own sensitivity ($1.0bn = +$9.5) implies about +$7.5 at $1.1bn.
disagreements.evidence: IREN FY26 release (Q4 SG&A $128.3m; FY26 $449.1m; adjusted EBITDA bridge); Q4 FY26 call (Q1 cash SG&A +$40-50m); CoreWeave FY2025 results (S&M $144m, G&A $651m on $5.13bn revenue).

disagreements.positions: First re-lease relative to the new-contract level per MW: A1 0.70; A2 about 0.50 (flat to 0.42 at age 6); A3 about 0.54-0.61; A4 about 0.66-0.74 for new cohorts and 0.76-0.86 for 2026 cohorts (spot/contract-share x 0.85); A5 about 0.58-0.63 on each cohort's own price.
disagreements.resolution: Kept the round-3 evidence band, central 0.60 at first re-lease (age 3-4), falling 12-15% a year. H100 at about 3.5 years is about 0.63 of new-generation per-MW pricing; A100 at about 6 years is 0.37-0.51 (Silicon Data/Ornn). Today's prices come from a supply-constrained market (3-year pricing up about 125% since Nov-2025 per IREN), so the top of the band should not be the base. Adjustments: A1 about -$4.5 and A4 about -$9 (tails above the band); A2 about +$5 on existing cohorts (below the band); A3 and A5 roughly unchanged.
disagreements.evidence: Round-3 verified Silicon Data H100 $2.77 / A100 $1.58; agent gpu_life blocks; Q4 FY26 call pricing remarks.

disagreements.topic: Agent 3's $2.0bn unattributed FY27 capex line versus the FY27 guide
disagreements.positions: A3 plugs $2.0bn of FY27 spend with no revenue to bring its bottom-up (~$22bn if all sites contract) up to the $25bn low end of the guide, plus $0.8bn FY27 and $1.0bn FY28 development. Its own bridge shows the plug alone costs -$4.9/share. A1 does the same with $1.3bn charged at WACC. A2 charges $1.4bn of FY27 Sweetwater works explicitly to S11/S12.
disagreements.resolution: Part of the line is real spend but mis-specified. The CFO says the $25-30bn includes Microsoft delivery, 2026-ARR deployments, 2027 air-cooled GPU and DC, liquid-cooled DC at Childress and Sweetwater 1, 'as well as earlier stage investment for 2028 and beyond', and that 'data center CapEx is running a year or two ahead of delivery'. That makes the balance early DC and substation spend on the 2028+ sites (and the BC 2027 headroom deployments, F09), not dead money. It should sit in the pipeline sites as capex spent early, recovered if the site is built (p about 0.4-0.5 for Sweetwater) and lost otherwise, plus the time cost. The guide is also the company's all-contracted plan, while A3 probability-weights its other 2027 GPU capex, so plugging to its low end at 100% is inconsistent. A3 also says the line holds the BC headroom spend while giving that capacity no revenue. Reclassified, the line costs about -$3.4/share, not -$4.9 (+$1.5 to +$2 to A3). A1's $1.3bn line gets the same treatment (about +$1).
disagreements.evidence: Q4 FY26 call, CFO capex paragraph and CEO remark on DC capex timing (stockanalysis transcript 662889-q4-2026); A3 revisions bridge.

disagreements.positions: Microsoft 6.75% (A3) or 7.0% (others); NVIDIA 7.0% (A3) or 7.5%; non-IG AI developers 10.0% (all); everything else 11% (A3, A4) or 11.5%.
disagreements.resolution: Sound and anchored. Microsoft: verified $3.65bn facility, Fitch A / DBRS A(low), blended 6.00% (USPP SOFR+2.13% equivalent, DDTL SOFR+2.25%), funding 96% of $5.81bn GPU capex with the prepayment. Adding 0.75-1.0pp for H2-4 completion and SLA risk on the equity slice is reasonable. Non-IG: verified 9.0% fixed $2.4bn Blue Owl/PIMCO facility, so 10% sits between that and WACC. NVIDIA 7.0-7.5% with no facility closed is fair. All five apply the low rates only inside signed terms, including committed capex and prepayment credits; tails, refreshes, uncontracted builds, pipeline and terminal stay at WACC. The split adds only +$0.6 to +$1.5/share, because in-term cash flows roughly repay the GPU capex.
disagreements.evidence: Jun-1-2026 IREN financing release (stocktitan, verified 2-Oct); FY26 release (9.0% fixed Blue Owl/PIMCO $2.4bn, verified).

confidence_reason: I settled three DCF inputs on primary evidence: GPU capex at 2.2x revenue from IREN's own orders, about $1.0-1.2bn of corporate cost, and a 0.60 first re-lease. I also verified the 6.00% A-rated and 9.0% non-IG financings. These lower the long-run DCF but not the 12-month drivers, and the agents already give the DCF only 25-50% weight. thesis_break_reason: Unchanged. At $21 the diluted market cap is about $9.5bn on about 450m shares, roughly 2.7x the $4bn of 2026 contracted ARR and about 27% below the $28.93 52-week low. Trading there would most likely mean distressed FY27 funding of the $25-30bn capex, a Horizon 2-4 miss beyond the Q2-2027 grace period, a customer default, or 2027 capacity signing well below $20m/MW. The round-4 site and discount-rate work changes long-run value, not this signal.
key_drivers: GPU capex per $ of annual revenue: IREN's orders imply 2.2-2.35x on market-priced deals (3.0x on Microsoft). At 2.2x a GPU cycle earns about WACC, so the DCF is near or below zero; at 1.7-1.8x it is +$8-13. This is now the single largest input (A4: about $5/share per $1m/MW of GPU cost).
Funding the $25-30bn FY27 capex: $14bn in hand, about $8bn more GPU financing and prepayments targeted, and the rest from DC financing and ATM equity. Shares about 555-595m by Oct-2027.
Horizon 2-4 acceptance (Q4 CY2026, grace to the start of Q2 2027) and NVIDIA commissioning (early 2027), taking contracted ARR from $1bn operating to about $4.7bn.
Price and terms on the uncontracted 2027 capacity (S04, S05, S09, S10; 456MW IT): management cites ~$25m/MW talks (unverified). Air-cooled retrofits clear WACC; new liquid builds roughly break even.
How the market capitalises contracted NTM EBITDA (CoreWeave about 7.5x): the bridges average $37 at 7.5x, which carries the stock while the DCF does not.

fair_value.reason: Agents' round-4 blends average $22.7. On common settled inputs (GPU capex 2.2x revenue, corporate about $1.0-1.2bn, first re-lease 0.60, A3's guide-gap line reclassified, contract rates as used), the split-rate DCFs come to about A1 -$16, A2 -$3, A3 -$6, A4 -$5, A5 -$9.5 (central about -$7; about +$5 to -$9 at the 2.0x management-payback bound). EV/EBITDA at 7.5x averages $37.4. 0.4 x -$7 + 0.6 x $37.4 is about $20 ($22 if the DCF is floored at zero for limited liability). Uses about 450m diluted shares today and 555-595m at Oct-2027, with customer prepayments as debt.

round4_review.split_vs_single_note: The split rate adds only +$0.6 to +$1.5 per share in every model: in-term contracted cash flows roughly repay the GPU and DC capex still to be spent on them, so a lower rate on them moves little. round4_review.what_drives_value_most: GPU capex per $ of annual revenue. On IREN's own deals (2.2-2.35x market, 3.0x Microsoft) a refresh or new GPU cycle earns about WACC, so the DCF equity is about zero to negative after corporate cost and debt-like claims. Each 0.1x is worth roughly $4-5/share. Next come the first re-lease level (about $6-10/share per 0.10) and corporate cost (about $9 per $0.5bn/yr). Contract discount rates and economic life are second order. The stock's value rests on how the market capitalises contracted EBITDA ($33-41 at 7.5x), not on the DCF.

summary: Round 4 rebuilt every DCF site by site from the checked inventory and split discounting. All five now carry the 17 sites once, with NVIDIA outside the $4bn and Sweetwater 1 phase 1 inside 0.8GW, and all use well-anchored contract rates (Microsoft about 7% on the verified A-rated 6.00% facility; non-IG 10% on the verified 9% paper). Settled on IREN's own orders (2.2x), cash SG&A (about $1.0-1.2bn at scale) and the 0.60 re-lease evidence, the DCFs reconcile to about -$16 to -$3 (central -$7; single-rate about $1 lower).
